Title: September 24, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Study Session

Topic1.Title: Boulder Valley School District Resilient School Plan and City Property Discussion
Topic1.Summary: Council Member Benjamin raised community concerns about the Boulder Valley School District passing a resilient school plan affecting school properties. City Manager Nuria Rivera-Vandermyde explained the city has no decision-making role over the properties but is discussing with the district potential city uses such as a police substation or training center. She noted the district has been a strong partner on aquatics and that the city will report back if any proposals come forward.

Topic2.Title: Public Safety Update: Policing
Topic2.Summary: Police Chief Steve Redford presented staffing levels, noting 12 sworn officer vacancies and about 30 positions not deployable as solo officers, with recruitment ongoing. Crime data showed decreases in property and person crimes except assaults, which are rising, alongside increased proactive policing. The chief highlighted the new Public Safety Information Center, community engagement efforts, and community satisfaction survey results showing 85% satisfaction. Council members asked about retention challenges, the Community Connect camera program, emoto and e-bike enforcement, and the status of the CARE team.

Topic3.Title: Public Safety Update: Police Oversight
Topic3.Summary: Independent Police Monitor Sherri Dye presented data on oversight complaints, classifications, and allegations, with 149 allegations in 2025 and 18 sustained. She explained the demographic breakdown of complainants and noted significant panel turnover since 2024. Panel co-chairs Lizzie Friend and Bill De La Cruz raised concerns that recent process changes have limited panel review of cases and asked for a clearer role in complaint handling. The five-year review of the oversight system is underway with a report expected in October.

Topic4.Title: Public Safety Update: Legal and Judicial System
Topic4.Summary: Presiding Judge Jeff Khan reviewed municipal court data on unhoused defendants, community court dismissals, warrants, and young adult cases such as minor-in-possession, nuisance party, and fraudulent ID charges. He explained that many public safety issues discussed fall under state court jurisdiction rather than municipal court. Council members asked about enforcement of large amplified parties on the Hill, the consequences for repeated camping violations, and how outcomes for trespass and other offenses compare to traffic cases.

Topic5.Title: Sister Cities Program Resolution and Process Update
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented a proposed update to Resolution 631 to clarify application submission, review, approval, annual reporting, and processes for inactive or discontinued alliances. Research with other municipalities found no dedicated staff or funding and varied approaches to limits and deactivation. Staff recommended an online application, clear review timelines, deadlines for council consideration, standardized agreements, and a possible cap and formal deactivation process. Council generally supported a council committee to oversee the program, with a cap to be recommended by the committee and revisions brought back for consent agenda approval.
